specification.problem: Estimate Inf_i(f)=Pr_x[f(x)!=f(x xor e_i)] for a chosen variable i of an n-variable Boolean function f. The method is a Hadamard-test (interference) readout on one ancilla using a phase oracle. It is a deliberately different readout from the abstract's Bernstein-Vazirani (BV) position-i sampling.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny instance: n=3 with a fixed hidden f, one target variable i (0-indexed), n+1=4 qubits. It covers the single-variable ancilla circuit, the shot-based estimator, and the thresholding rule for juntas. The BV-output-position circuit, the paper's approximation algorithm, the probabilistic junta-learning algorithms, the comparison with Floess et al., and the final truth-table learning step are outside this scope.

symbols.meaning: index of the target variable; input qubit i (little-endian) holds x_i

symbols.domain: unitary on n qubits, opaque placeholder gate

symbols.meaning: Pauli X on input qubit i, so X_i|x>=|x xor e_i>
junta size (f depends on at most k variables)

equations.label: Influence definition
equations.description: Influence as the probability that flipping bit i changes f, rewritten with the +/-1 correlation.
equations.justification: The abstract equates the dependence degree with the influence. The exact formula is the standard definition, supplied as an assumption.
assumptions: The influence is the probability definition for Boolean f.

equations.label: Circuit state before the final Hadamard
equations.description: The ancilla is in |+>. The circuit CX(a->i), U_f, CX(a->i) acts on |+>_a|s>. Branch 0 applies U_f. Branch 1 applies X_i U_f X_i. Only one oracle placement is needed because U_f is applied unconditionally.
equations.justification: This is the proposed construction from the method sketch. The sketch counts 2 queries per run, but a controlled-X conjugation around a single U_f gives the same state with 1 query.
assumptions: CX gates are ordinary gates and are not queries.
U_f is supplied as a phase oracle.

equations.label: Interference overlap
equations.description: Since X_i|s>=|s>, the overlap is a real correlation of f with its i-th shift.
equations.justification: Direct calculation from U_f|s>=2^{-n/2} sum_x (-1)^{f(x)}|x> and the definition of X_i.

equations.label: Ancilla readout probability
equations.description: After H on the ancilla, P(a=1) equals the influence, read from one ancilla bit.
equations.abstract_quote: the probability of getting a 1 in each position $i$ is equal to the dependence degree of $f$ on the variable $x_{i}$
equations.justification: The abstract states the BV-position claim. This circuit reproduces the same probability through an ancilla, which is an inference and not the paper's circuit. The value follows from eq_3.
assumptions: The ancilla is measured in the computational basis after H.

equations.label: Shot count and junta thresholding
equations.description: Hoeffding bound for the empirical frequency p-hat of ancilla=1. The threshold tau is set below the minimum nonzero influence of a k-junta, with eps<tau.
equations.justification: Standard Hoeffding bound. The junta gap is taken from the sketch's assumption of at least 2^-k (a k-junta's nonzero influence is a multiple of 2^{1-k}, so it is at least 2^{1-k}). The exact threshold rule is not from the abstract.
assumptions: Choose eps < tau, for example eps=2^{-k-1}.

registers.name: x
registers.role: input register; qubit j holds x_j (little-endian); H^n gives |s>

registers.name: a
registers.role: interference ancilla, initially |+>; the CX control and the measured qubit

registers.name: c
registers.role: records the ancilla outcome; measure(a,0), so counts key '1' means a=1

specification.initial_state: |0>^{n}|0>_a, then H on all n+1 qubits, giving |s>|+>_a.

steps.description: Prepare |s> by applying H to every input qubit and prepare the ancilla in |+> with H.
Apply CX with control a and target input qubit i.
Apply the opaque phase-oracle placeholder U_f once to the input register. This is 1 query per run.
Apply CX with control a and target input qubit i again, giving the state in eq_2.
Apply H to the ancilla and measure only the ancilla into classical bit 0. Do not measure the input register.
Repeat for N shots and set p-hat to the fraction of outcomes with a=1. For juntas, repeat over all i and keep those with p-hat > tau.

specification.measurement: Measure the ancilla qubit only, into classical bit 0. With Qiskit little-endian keys, read the single character of the counts key. P(1)=Inf_i.
specification.classical_postprocessing: p-hat = counts['1']/N is the estimate of Inf_i(f). For juntas, the relevant set is {i : p-hat_i > tau}. Learning f on the relevant variables by further queries is not specified here.
assumptions: Scope choice: n=3, one target variable, a fixed hidden f. The smallest useful instance is a choice of mine, not from the abstract.
The oracle is a phase oracle. A bit oracle would need a |-> ancilla and one more qubit.
The influence is the probability definition.
The CX gates are standard and are not oracle queries.
The method is a deliberately different readout from the abstract's BV-based algorithm.
The junta gap and threshold rule are assumptions.
